answer: One agent may register one marble loom, locking a 90-credit bond and taking an ivory shuttle. The loom log publishes thread lot, count per metre, and length. An auditor recomputes use as length times count; a shortfall, reused lot, or mismatched key burns the bond. The first loom pays 29, the k-th pays 29+6(k-1), and the 1,000th pays 6,023, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,026,000 in fees plus 90,000 locked. A rented-loom ring fails: the rented loom is already logged, so a second claim with the same shuttle or lot burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 29 once and recovers 90 after a clean epoch.
